newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up, despite monetary tightening.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up, despite monetary tightening.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed ahead in moderate trade despite a modest tightening of monetary policy, traders said.
"There continues to be strong buying of selective stocks," Delta brokerage trader Eduardo Soto.
The bolsa's 19-share index ended up 0.75 percent at 9521.74 points, despite a new Central Bank ruling that requires commercial banks to place 15 percent of their deposits in a Central Bank account.
Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez said the move would mop-up over 165 billion bolivars ($337 million) from Venezuela's overly liquid money markets and help firm interest rates.

Textiles and fiberglass company Sudamtex Type II shares led gainers, ending ahead 5.49 percent at 48.00 bolivars, as a total of 53 million shares worth 8.8 billion bolivars ($18 million) were exchanged.
Among traded issues, 25 rose, 12 fell and seven closed flat.
